verified_key_information_units.information: Headline financial performance showing net sales decreased to SEK 295M (from SEK 352M in 2024) with EBITDA of SEK 17M (third consecutive positive year but down from SEK 47M), EBIT loss of SEK 40M (compared to SEK 4M loss in 2024), and operating cash flow turning negative at SEK -73M (from SEK 57M in 2024), while cash reserves declined to SEK 30M.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Financial highlights table (page 5), Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income (page 33), Consolidated Balance Sheet (page 34), Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows (page 36)

candidate_sentences.text: Net sales fell 16% to SEK 295.3 million from SEK 352.9 million, while total revenue declined to SEK 337.8 million from SEK 408.8 million.
EBITDA remained positive for the third consecutive year but decreased to SEK 17.5 million from SEK 46.7 million.
EBIT deteriorated to a loss of SEK 40.0 million from SEK 4.0 million, and the loss after tax widened to SEK 46.6 million from SEK 5.7 million.
Operating cash flow fell sharply to an outflow of SEK 72.6 million from an inflow of SEK 56.8 million.
Cash and cash equivalents declined to SEK 30.1 million from SEK 49.7 million, although the available overdraft facility increased from SEK 30 million to SEK 50 million and was undrawn at year-end.

verified_key_information_units.information: Business restructuring into two segments (Products & Missions and Data & Services) to enhance operational efficiency, with Data & Services segment growing net sales by approximately 80% to SEK 80M (from SEK 45M in 2024) driven by recurring maritime data revenues from operational Sedna satellites.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Operations section (page 9-11), CEO Review (page 6), Business segments highlights (page 11)

candidate_sentences.text: The deterioration was concentrated in Products & Missions, where net sales fell to SEK 245.0 million from SEK 346.0 million and EBITDA to SEK 16.8 million from SEK 51.6 million.
Data & Services developed positively, with sales increasing by 80% to SEK 80.1 million and EBITDA rising to SEK 27.8 million from SEK 21.1 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Major contract acquisitions including ESA's INFLECION Phase 1 agreement (part of a SEK 350M co-funded program with 50% UK Space Agency contribution) and SEK 11.8M order for EPS-Sterna weather constellation components, significantly boosting order backlog and providing multi-year revenue visibility.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: 2025 in brief (page 5), Board of Directors' Report (page 32), Significant events during the year (page 32)

candidate_sentences.text: Operationally, Sedna-1 and Sedna-2 became fully operational, supporting recurring maritime data revenues, while assembly began on the VIREON Earth Observation constellation and the INFLECION Phase 1 contract was signed.
After year-end, AAC received its largest order to date: a EUR 76.3 million, approximately SEK 820 million, contract for 20 EPS-Sterna microwave radiometers.

verified_key_information_units.information: Key operational milestones: Sedna-1 and Sedna-2 satellites became fully operational strengthening maritime AIS network capacity; first CubeCAT laser communication terminals delivered enabling high-speed optical links; assembly commenced on first two VIREON™ Earth Observation satellites for 2026 launch.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: 2025 in brief (page 5), Weather technology praised by ESA section (page 5), Operations structured in two segments (page 5), Board of Directors' Report (page 32)

candidate_sentences.text: Operationally, Sedna-1 and Sedna-2 became fully operational, supporting recurring maritime data revenues, while assembly began on the VIREON Earth Observation constellation and the INFLECION Phase 1 contract was signed.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic institutional investment by Bonnier Capital of up to SEK 140M (with SEK 50.3M initial tranche completed in December 2025) strengthening ownership base and securing funding for satellite constellation development and data services expansion.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Institutional ownership strengthened section (page 5), Board of Directors' Report (page 32), Top 10 shareholders table (page 18)

verified_key_information_units.information: Market positioning leveraged through AI-enhanced space-based data services and vertical integration in satellite manufacturing, with focus shifting toward recurring revenue streams from operational constellations rather than project-based hardware sales.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO Review (page 6), Invest in AAC Clyde Space section (page 8), Business model description (page 9-10)

verified_key_information_units.information: Liquidity management via expanded overdraft facility to SEK 50M (from SEK 30M) and maintained equity ratio of 80% (up from 71% in 2024), ensuring financial stability despite cash flow pressures from program delays and investment requirements.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Cash flow, liquidity and financial position section (page 33), Consolidated Balance Sheet (page 34), Significant events during the year (page 32)

candidate_sentences.text: Cash and cash equivalents declined to SEK 30.1 million from SEK 49.7 million, although the available overdraft facility increased from SEK 30 million to SEK 50 million and was undrawn at year-end.
The equity ratio improved to 80% from 71%, supported by two directed share issues that raised approximately SEK 114.8 million before issue costs.

verified_key_information_units.information: Material post-reporting-period events: successful launch and commissioning of VIREON™-1 and VIREON™-2 Earth Observation satellites; initiation of Sedna-3 and Sedna-4 maritime satellite construction; receipt of EUR 76.3M order from OHB Sweden for 20 EPS-Sterna microwave radiometers.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Significant events after the end of the year (page 32, 36), Board of Directors' Report (page 32)

candidate_sentences.text: After year-end, AAC received its largest order to date: a EUR 76.3 million, approximately SEK 820 million, contract for 20 EPS-Sterna microwave radiometers.
This increased the order backlog to approximately SEK 1.1 billion by the end of March 2026 and improved the Group’s forward financial visibility.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K4, K7 and K8 are fully represented. K3 is only partially covered (INFLECION and EPS-Sterna mentioned but without the SEK 350M co-funded programme detail or SEK 11.8M order). K5 and K6 are entirely absent.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. Each sentence follows logically from the preceding ones, with clear cause-and-effect relationships (e.g., programme delays explaining revenue declines in [S8]–[S10] and their impact on cash flow in [S11]). Segment performance is presented separately without any claim that the figures must arithmetically sum to the consolidated totals. No self-contradictions, logical gaps, or unnecessary repetitions are present, and the overall structure moves logically from financial results to operational developments and post-year-end events.
